source.title: Theory of Deep Learning III : explaining the non-overfitting puzzle by
source.authors: T. Poggio; Kenji Kawaguchi; Q. Liao; B. Miranda; Lorenzo Rosasco; Xavier Boix; J. Hidary; H. Mhaskar

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, including supplementary information. Some results are described only in figures.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own CIFAR training experiments and classification-error outcomes relevant to V1, but does not explicitly replicate one of the original studies.
record.gate_note: The authors cite Zhang et al. for prior results; those cited results are not rows. The paper's own CIFAR experiments and figure descriptions provide the extracted results. It states that tricks were turned off except for batch normalization in CIFAR experiments.
record.test_reason: The paper reports its own convolutional-network training classification errors on CIFAR, including scrambled labels and an SGD parameter-count sweep. These use the same broad method and measure as V1's original experiments; the GD and polynomial-network experiments provide additional settings. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate but understates the central contribution: the authors propose a local equivalence between deep-network gradient dynamics near stable global minima and degenerate linear gradient systems. Under assumptions on minima and datasets, they use this to explain implicit regularization and why test loss can overfit while test classification error does not. They do not establish general convergence from random initialization to global minima.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses GD for its perturbation experiment and reports CIFAR experiments with a small all-convolutional network; it turns off data augmentation and regularization, while retaining batch normalization in CIFAR experiments. It does not identify these experiments as an explicit replication of a named original source.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper varies training-set size and model parameter count in separate CIFAR figure experiments; the reported perturbation outcome follows repeated Gaussian weight perturbations and further GD.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors argue that local gradient dynamics near stable global minima resemble a degenerate linear system, and that implicit regularization and margin maximization explain classification generalization despite overfitting of the loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the authors' assumptions on empirical minima and datasets, overparameterization can increase test loss without increasing test classification error.

record.problems: Some CIFAR findings are presented through plots without precise numeric values in the supplied text. The paper focuses on GD rather than SGD in its analysis, and notes that its assumptions and conclusions concern stable zero-loss minima and suitable datasets.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100 is not explicitly identified; Adam, initialization dependence, and controlled comparisons of early stopping or explicit regularization are not tested. The supplied text does not establish SGD specifically for the random-label result.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local-minimum frequencies and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Training degradation across depth, identity-shortcut comparisons, very deep tanh initialization, and Fixup.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons, signal and gradient propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to a stability threshold, catapult dynamics, edge-of-stability training, and divergence.
Batch-normalized versus unnormalized training speed and learning-rate tolerance; Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: Normally labeled CIFAR training classification error across training-subset sizes, paired with the scrambled-label experiment. Section 2 explicitly describes zero training error in the fitting regime.

ReLU-network training classification error across parameter counts on 50,000 CIFAR-10 examples, using SGD with batch size 100 for 70 epochs. This is the clearest explicitly specified SGD experiment and supplies the smaller-versus-larger model comparison. Curve values cannot be recovered from the supplied text, so no additional verdict is assigned.

Polynomial-network training classification errors for normally labeled and scrambled-label CIFAR subsets. These conditions are not represented by R3's parameter-count sweep. Numerical values require the figure.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text omits most plotted curves. No numerical values or failure rates were inferred from axes alone. Batch normalization is retained in CIFAR experiments, but its presence without a comparison does not test V6. Training-loss overfitting and weight-perturbation recovery do not test V5.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes; the paper says data augmentation and regularization were absent in the cited figure setups.
The paper does not run the teacher-student ReLU experiment or vary student width.
The paper does not compare plain and residual networks across depth or test the named shortcut and normalization conditions.
The paper does not compare initialization methods or test trainable depth.
The paper does not sweep learning rates around a stability limit or measure sharpness.
The paper does not compare batch-normalized and unnormalized networks for training speed or learning-rate tolerance.

rows.note: The text describes the right plot as the same network trained on randomly scrambled labels; the caption and surrounding text identify zero training error on randomly labeled data. The exact plotted value is not stated.

rows.subject: 5-layer convolutional neural network with 16, 32, 64 and 128 feature maps in hidden layers
rows.operation_detail: Trained with gradient descent on CIFAR-10 crossentropy; after reaching zero training classification error, weights were repeatedly perturbed and training continued.

conditions.value: Gaussian noise, standard deviation 1/4 of corresponding layer weights
every 100 training epochs after initial convergence

rows.measure: Training classification error after perturbation and subsequent training
rows.value: training error reset to zero after added perturbations
rows.note: Initial convergence was after roughly 1800 epochs of GD. The paper describes the repeated perturbation protocol and says training loss returned to its original level and training error reset to zero.
rows.check: The initial attainment of zero training classification error after roughly 1800 GD epochs directly bears on V1 and should be recorded separately from recovery after perturbation. Recovery also reaches zero, but does not establish convergence from random initialization. Batch normalization was retained.
